sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Achintya Bhedabheda**: The core philosophy of Chaitanya, meaning 'Inconceivable Oneness and Difference' between the individual soul (Jiva) and the Supreme (Krishna).
• **Sankirtana Movement**: The revolutionary practice of public congregational chanting of the Holy Names, which bypassed caste and ritualistic barriers.
• **Gaudiya Vaishnavism**: The specific school of Vaishnavism centered on the worship of Radha and Krishna as the supreme divine couple.
• **Key Metric**: Chaitanya's movement was unique in its emotional intensity ('Prema-bhakti') and its rejection of the rigid caste-based hierarchy of the Brahminical orthodoxy.

items.definition: Congregational chanting of the names of God; served as a tool for mass mobilization and social leveling.
The birthplace of Chaitanya and the epicenter of his early movement; a major center of Sanskrit learning.
A Muslim-born disciple of Chaitanya, often called 'Namacharya', highlighting the movement's secular/inclusive nature.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Democratization of Religion**: Removed the monopoly of the priestly class over spiritual salvation.
• **Literary Contribution**: Inspired the 'Chaitanya Charitamrita' by Krishnadasa Kaviraja, a primary source for his life.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Resistance from orthodox Smarta Brahmins and the challenge of maintaining doctrinal purity.
• **Solutions**: Institutionalization through the 'Six Goswamis of Vrindavan' who codified the theology.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-A-S-H' (Chaitanya, Achintya, Sankirtana, Haridas).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Chaitanya preached Achintya Bhedabheda, popularized Sankirtana, and accepted Haridas (a Muslim) as a top disciple.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Chaitanya with the 'Varkari' movement saints. Remember: Chaitanya is Gaudiya (Bengal/Odisha), while Varkari (Tukaram/Namdev) is Maharashtra.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Radical Humanism' when describing Chaitanya's impact on the caste system.

keyTakeaways: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was a contemporary of the early Mughal period (Lodi/Babur era).
His philosophy of Achintya Bhedabheda is a unique synthesis of monism and dualism.
The movement was a major force in social integration, transcending religious and caste boundaries.
